images.prompt:
Create one premium photorealistic Dogs field-guide portrait: a mature Heideterrier, the German Lüneburg Heath working hunting population. Use ONLY this independently written factual anatomy description; no reference photograph is provided or requested.

A medium compact strong dog of roughly50cm withers scale, body a little longer than tall, deep well-sprung chest, strong level back, muscular flat croup, and modest abdominal tuck-up. Broad flat skull tapering mildly between eyes, substantial muzzle slightly shorter than skull with strong chin and tight dark lips, black nose, small oval dark eyes. High-set V-shaped ears fold close to the sides of the head. Strong moderately short neck and muscular shoulders. Straight strong-boned forelegs; broad close-toed front paws. Muscular thighs, sound bent stifles, low hocks, short rear pasterns, and compact oval hindpaws. Dense coarse smooth black coat with tan eyebrow spots, muzzle areas, modest chest patches and lower legs. A complete natural tapering tail attached at the croup extends behind horizontally with a gentle sickle; never a tail curled over the back. Avoid long narrow hound muzzle, drooping long ears, extreme Dobermann slenderness, very short legs, juvenile proportions or exaggerated hair.

Invent a fresh composition: one anonymous adult dog standing relaxed in a left-facing three-quarter side view, head turned just enough to show both eyes, mouth softly closed. Four anatomically coherent separated paws bear weight on clear firm pale sand, with natural contact shadows; full connected tail and free tip remain visible. A quiet Lüneburg Heath clearing with sparse dry autumn heath at the edges, a few distant birches and soft early morning light. Restrained natural colours, realistic coat texture, calm field photography, no dramatic sky or dense pink flower slope. Do not recreate any existing photograph, named dog, pose or distinctive arrangement.

profileEvidence.summary: Bold, energetic and willing to work with a handler, the Heideterrier was developed for the demanding job of flushing wild boar. Its breeding club puts practical hunting ability and stamina at the centre of selection. Karl-Heinz Markhoff and Hans-Werner Jahnke began developing the type in Germany's Lüneburg Heath during the 1970s.
profileEvidence.shortDescription: A bold, energetic Lüneburg Heath hunting dog, selected for wild-boar work, stamina and cooperation with its handler.
